verdict.rationale: Jitsu's core function delivers your event data and profiles into destinations you own: Postgres, S3, GCS, ClickHouse, BigQuery, Snowflake and others. It is also 100% open source and self-hostable, and its Management API covers workspace configuration, so data already lives outside the vendor and leaving is feasible. However, no documented 'export everything' feature or explicit open-format guarantee exists for configuration or other account data. missing for 10: an explicit full-account data export feature, documented open export formats (e.g., Parquet/CSV/JSON) for all data including configs, offboarding/leave documentation, and independent hands-on corroboration of migrating away.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: Make your data warehouse the single source of truth for your data.
Delivery to destinations — ClickHouse, BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, Postgres, S3, GCS, and dozens of SaaS tools
Profiles are customer records stored in your warehouse, based on the events data you send to Jitsu.
Jitsu is 100% open-source and can be deployed to any on-premise infrastructure.
Jitsu exposes an HTTP API for managing workspaces, sites, destinations, connections, syncs and functions.
